P-299 (merged 2026-09-17, engine main `3809275f`) already pinned the engine to `@empressaio/setback-corpus@1.4.0` exactly and measured the distance the pin closed (87 districts the corpus had and the engine did not, 9 renames, 56 changed-field districts, 91 per-field state transitions).

preRegisteredPredictions.quoted: A Hays boundary-edge fixture resolves a setback table through the corpus (the 'No setback table configured' string does not appear), and a city with genuinely no table still says so.
preRegisteredPredictions.whatWouldProveItWrong: The missing-table string still appearing on a corpus-served Hays city, OR a table-less city now resolving a table (which would mean the fix papered over the absence instead of naming it).

preRegisteredPredictions.quoted: Editing one side of the setback pair alone makes the divergence test fail.
preRegisteredPredictions.whatWouldProveItWrong: A corpus key added and served by nobody that the test still passes on (registry not total), or an engine row naming a key the corpus does not carry that the test still passes on.

preRegisteredPredictions.quoted: A writer asked to emit `no-buildable-area` with an 'unzoned' reason fails a test.
preRegisteredPredictions.whatWouldProveItWrong: A guard that passes the unzoned case, or one that refuses EVERY no-buildable-area including a genuine computed zero (a guard that cannot discriminate is not the guard R4 asked for).

preRegisteredPredictions.quoted: The P-263 dry run's per-county totals sum to the 490,185 population, with every atom in exactly one bucket, and the run writes nothing (prove it by reading the store after).
preRegisteredPredictions.whatWouldProveItWrong: A population whose buckets do not sum, an atom in two buckets, or a store digest that changes between the census's own two reads.

preRegisteredPredictions.statement: The registry is TOTAL over the corpus universe: 43 rows for 43 corpus keys at `@empressaio/setback-corpus@1.4.0`, 14 `served: true`, 29 `served: false` split 2 withheld + 27 not wired. Predicted BEFORE the divergence test was run against the built package. A row count other than 43 means the engine is keyed on something other than the corpus's own list.

The pre-P-260 lookup surface (15 keys, `VENDORED_JURISDICTION_KEYS`) is preserved exactly: `SETBACK_LOOKUP_KEYS` still answers 15 keys (14 corpus-served + the `elgin-tx` alias), so this change does not silently add or drop a served jurisdiction while claiming to only re-source the list.

NOT all 490,185 atoms are classifiable from their reason. The dispatch's own two figures (208,868 unzoned + 153,775 not onboarded = 362,643) leave 127,542 atoms whose reason is neither. Prediction: `unclassifiedByReason` is a NON-EMPTY bucket of roughly that remainder (some of it the Tier-1 bake's own 'Tier-1 snapshot status no-buildable-area' reason and the geometry-verify failures), and it is reported as movement the change cannot make rather than folded into either class. A census whose three buckets sum to the population but whose unclassified bucket is ~0 would mean the classifier over-claims, not that the population is clean.

Zero atoms in the six counties carry a `zero` proof today (predicted `alreadyComputedZero` = 0). If any atom does carry one, the pre-P-263 type was already being violated in the other direction and the census must say so — the population definition would then have to exclude them explicitly, which it does.

The P-260 registry table is measured, not asserted: for every wired city the cohort count is read from the atoms store and the ledger count from the ledger store, and a city whose two numbers disagree is reported as a finding rather than reconciled by choosing one. Where a city has no landed table the row carries the `tableNotLandedReason` produced by `resolveSetbackCityBinding` — a silent blank is a defect, so a row with neither a table nor a reason fails this lane's own report.

The store read is ONE leased window. P-307's key rule means the atoms endpoint (`ep-lucky-truth-apodo8hr...`) is the SAME physical store the publish job leases for `PRODUCTION_HAUSKA_MCP_URL:production`; at 2026-09-17T20:28Z the lease was held by `factory-bastrop-publish-sxv8r` until 20:57:46Z, and this lane takes (not bypasses) the lease when it frees. If it is renewed, the census is deferred and the deferral is reported rather than the read being run beside a writer.

p260Changes: packages/adapters/src/local/setbacks/index.ts — the hand-kept `VENDORED_JURISDICTION_KEYS` (15 keys) is GONE. The corpus supplies the key universe; this file supplies POLICY, and policy is total: `SETBACK_ENGINE_REGISTRY` maps every corpus key to a row (served + routing arm, or not served + a reason drawn from `SETBACK_NOT_SERVED_REASON`). `SETBACK_TABLES` is built from `SETBACK_LOOKUP_KEYS` (served keys + the `elgin-tx` alias), so the resolved table set is unchanged while its provenance is the corpus.
packages/adapters/src/index.ts — the registry, its row types and `listNotServedSetbackJurisdictions()` are exported, so a caller can ask what is NOT served instead of inferring it from a null.

packages/engine-core/src/setback-writer/city-binding.ts — `SetbackCityBinding.tableNotLandedReason` (non-null exactly when `tableLanded` is false). It distinguishes the four real cases: authored from a live per-parcel record by R13 (no table row is expected), withheld by standing ruling, wired-in-engine-but-not-served (a registry gap), or genuinely absent from the corpus (not yet researched).
p263Changes: packages/atoms/src/property-instances.ts — `EnvelopeHonestOutcome`'s `no-buildable-area` arm now REQUIRES `zero: BuildableEnvelopeZeroProof` (method + `areaSqFt: 0` + the atom it rests on). The claim cannot be typed without its computation.

packages/engine-core/src/property-reasoning/envelope-outcome-honesty.ts (new) — one gate every writer calls: `assertEnvelopeOutcomeIsHonest` throws `ENVELOPE_OUTCOME_DISHONEST` (`NO_BUILDABLE_AREA_WITHOUT_ZERO`, `NO_BUILDABLE_AREA_WITH_ABSENCE_REASON`, `ZERO_PROOF_NOT_ZERO`); `classifyEnvelopeAbsenceReason` is the ONE classifier the guard and the census both read, so the instrument cannot disagree with the guard about what a reason means; `outcomeForEnvelopeDecline` maps a decline to `not-applicable` (unzoned) or `provisional-front-edge` (pending).

packages/engine-core/src/depth-warm/honest-decline-promote.ts — the decline writer no longer stamps `no-buildable-area` unconditionally: with a `zero` proof it claims the zero and carries it; without one it says `not-applicable` / `provisional-front-edge`.

packages/engine-core/src/property-reasoning/bake-from-tier1-snapshot.ts — the Tier-1 bake re-asserted an upstream STATUS ('Tier-1 snapshot status no-buildable-area') as its own computed zero. It now reports `provisional-front-edge` and names the upstream status instead of claiming it.
packages/engine-core/src/property-reasoning/emit-buildable-envelope.ts — the emitter passes every outcome through the gate before it persists anything.

packages/engine-core/scripts/p263-envelope-outcome-census.mts (new) — the dry run. Counting rule: active `buildable-envelope` atoms whose `parcelNodeId` prefix is one of the six counties, `outcome.kind = no-buildable-area`, no `zero` proof; bucketed by the shared classifier; a zero-carrying atom is EXCLUDED from the population and reported separately (`alreadyComputedZero`), and non-matching kinds are reported as `notNoBuildableArea`; the run asserts `population == bucketSum` and exits non-zero otherwise, and proves it wrote nothing by digesting the population before and after.

A guardrail that does not survive a clone is not a guardrail (DEV_PROCESS).
countingRules: Registry totality: count of `SETBACK_ENGINE_REGISTRY` rows vs count of `SETBACK_JURISDICTION_KEYS` from the corpus package — two different sources, compared by identity of keys, never by size alone.
P-263 movement: every figure is a `count(*)` sum over a `(county, kind, reason, has-zero)` grouping; the classifier is the same function the writer guard calls.
P-260 registry table: cohort count per city from the atoms store; ledger count per city from the ledger store; both figures travel with their own counting rule in the close.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A1 — does re-sourcing the KEY LIST change which jurisdictions the engine serves?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: P2. The served set is declared explicitly, not derived from the corpus's presence, so the change is provenance-only: 14 corpus-served keys + the `elgin-tx` alias = the same 15 lookups as before. `elgin-tx` is deliberately NOT a registry row because it is not a corpus key — a registry that invented rows for aliases would report a jurisdiction the corpus does not carry.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A2 — is 'not served' the same statement as 'no setback law'?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: No, and the design separates them by construction: `served: false` carries a reason that says which of the two it is (withheld by ruling vs not yet wired), and `city-binding.ts` says the same thing to a writer as `tableNotLandedReason`. The defect class this program hunts is a silent absence reading identically to 'not checked'; a registry row without a reason would recreate it.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A3 — could the honesty gate be a guard that cannot fire, or one that fires on everything?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: Both directions are pinned in the tests: the unzoned-reason and no-zero cases must THROW (falsifier 3), and a genuine computed zero must be ACCEPTED (the control). A gate that refused every `no-buildable-area` would delete the honest zero the serving path is allowed to print.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A4 — the mission says unzoned becomes `not-applicable` and 'not onboarded' becomes 'whatever the current ledger supports'. Is `provisional-front-edge` that?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: Held as the honest answer, not as a guess: a not-yet-onboarded jurisdiction is zoned land whose derivation is pending, so the engine may not claim either a zero or a scope statement. `provisional-front-edge` says pending; the LEDGER apply (operator-authorised, not this lane) decides what the cell becomes. If the operator rules that the not-onboarded cohort should read `not-applicable`, that is a one-line change in `outcomeForEnvelopeDecline` and it is named here as open.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A5 — where does the census's power to disagree with the guard come from?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: It cannot: the census imports `classifyEnvelopeAbsenceReason` from the same module the guard calls. Deliberate, because a second copy of a classification rule in another file drifts from the first (the same reasoning P-307 used for the lease key).

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A6 — what would make this lane's PR unsafe to merge?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: If the atom type change forces a writer to invent a zero to keep compiling, or if any consumer reads `no-buildable-area` and treats the absence of a zero as optional. The workspace-wide `tsc --noEmit` (all 20 packages, exit 0 at 2026-09-17T20:26Z) is the evidence the type is not being papered over; the serving-side readers are LDT/retrieval and are out of this lane's scope by the dispatch's 'Do not'.
